builder.empty: Nothing selected yet. Choose a template or tick components.
builder.heading: Build a scenario
builder.intro: Start from a template, or tick the components of your energy system.
builder.wip: Work in progress: every component has its settings form; the upload of time series follows. Until then you can see below what is still missing, and open a complete scenario file further down.
check.battery_no_source: {component} has nothing to charge from. Add a grid connection, PV or wind.
check.c_rate: {component}: the charge/discharge rate (C-rate) must be greater than 0.
check.capacity_factor: {component}: the generation profile has values up to {maximum}, but a capacity factor is at most 1 (output per installed kW). A profile downloaded for a larger system has to be divided by its size.
check.chp_efficiency_sum: {component}: electrical + thermal efficiency ({total}) cannot be greater than 1.
check.chp_no_heat_demand: {component} always produces heat as well. Without a heat demand the heat cannot be used and the plant will not run.
check.chp_only_heat_source: {component} is the only heat source and its electricity cannot be exported. If heat demand is high compared to electricity demand the model can become infeasible.
check.cop_missing: {component}: no COP time series uploaded. Upload a file or use a constant COP instead.
check.cop_not_positive: {component}: the constant COP must be greater than 0.
check.demand_no_supply: {component} has no supply. Add a grid connection (or PV or wind).
check.efficiency: {component}: the efficiency must be greater than 0.
check.efficiency_electrical: {component}: the electrical efficiency must be greater than 0.
check.efficiency_thermal: {component}: the thermal efficiency must be greater than 0.
check.feedin_above_lowest_price: The feed-in tariff ({tariff} €/kWh) is higher than the lowest electricity price in the series ({price} €/kWh). The model could buy and sell electricity at the same time for unlimited profit and cannot be solved. Please check the prices and their units.
check.feedin_above_price: The feed-in tariff ({tariff} €/kWh) is higher than the electricity price ({price} €/kWh). The model could buy and sell electricity at the same time for unlimited profit and cannot be solved. Please check the prices and their units.
check.feedin_unused: {component} is selected, but nothing feeds electricity into it.
check.fixed_needs_capacity: {component}: fixed mode needs a capacity greater than 0 (or set the mode to 'invest').
check.gas_unused: {component} is selected, but no component uses gas.
check.grid_price_empty: {component}: the price series contains empty values. Please check the selected column.
check.grid_price_missing: {component}: no price time series uploaded. Upload a file or use a constant price instead.
check.grid_price_short: {component}: the price series has {count} values, but the selected time range needs {needed}. Upload a longer series or shorten the time range.
check.heat_not_supplied: {component} cannot be supplied. It needs a working heat source: a gas boiler or CHP plant together with a gas import, or a heat pump or heating rod together with electricity from the grid or PV.
check.no_demand: No demand selected. Add an electricity demand or a heat demand.
check.no_fuel: {component} has no fuel supply and cannot run.
check.no_heat_demand: {component} is selected, but there is no heat demand.
check.profile_missing: {component}: no time series uploaded. Upload a time series for it.
check.profile_shares: {component}: the demand profile adds up to {total}, but shares of the annual demand must add up to 1 over a year. Check the profile, or choose 'The demand in kW'.
check.renewables_alone.one: {components} alone cannot cover demand at all times. Without a grid connection (or enough storage) the model may be infeasible.
check.renewables_alone.other: {components} alone cannot cover demand at all times. Without a grid connection (or enough storage) the model may be infeasible.
check.series_invalid: {component}: the selected time series contains empty or non-numeric values. Please check the selected column.
check.series_long: {component}: the time series has {count} values, but the selected time range needs {needed}. Only the first {needed} values will be used.
check.series_short: {component}: the time series has {count} values, but the selected time range needs {needed}. Upload a longer series or shorten the time range.
check.short_period_invest.one: {components} is in investment mode, but the scenario covers less than a year. Its size is only reliable for a whole year: the seasons differ, and the yearly cost of a plant is not scaled to a shorter period.
check.short_period_invest.other: {components} are in investment mode, but the scenario covers less than a year. Their sizes are only reliable for a whole year: the seasons differ, and the yearly cost of a plant is not scaled to a shorter period.
check.surplus_not_exported: Surplus electricity from {components} cannot be exported. With a fixed capacity the model can become infeasible when production is higher than what is used.
check.unbounded_plant: {component}: without an upper limit this plant earns more from feeding in than it costs ({margin} EUR per kW in the simulated period at a feed-in revenue of {revenue} EUR/kWh), so the optimization would build it without end. Set an upper limit for the plant or lower the feed-in revenue.

field.capacity.capacity.help: The installed peak power of the plant.
field.capacity.capacity.help@battery: The energy that the battery can store.
field.capacity.capacity.help@chp: The electrical output of the CHP plant. Its heat output follows from the efficiencies.
field.capacity.capacity.help@gas_boiler: The heat output of the boiler.
field.capacity.capacity.help@heat_pump: The heat output of the heat pump.
field.capacity.capacity.help@heat_storag: The heat that the heat storage can hold.
field.capacity.capacity.help@heating_rod: The heat output of the heating rod.
field.capacity.capacity.help@wind: The rated power of the wind turbine.
field.capacity.capacity.label: Installed size
field.capacity.capex.help: The total installed cost divided by the installed power, for example from a quote.
field.capacity.capex.help@battery: The total installed cost divided by the capacity, for example from a quote.
field.capacity.capex.help@heat_storage: The total installed cost divided by the capacity, for example from a quote.
field.capacity.capex.label: Investment cost
field.capacity.interest_rate.help: Used to spread the investment over its lifetime. 0 means no interest.
field.capacity.interest_rate.label: Interest rate
field.capacity.lifetime.help: How long the plant is used. The investment is spread over this time.
field.capacity.lifetime.label: Lifetime
field.capacity.maximum.help: Upper limit for the optimizer, for example from the available space. Leave empty for no limit.
field.capacity.maximum.help@pv: Upper limit for the optimizer, for example from the roof area. Leave empty for no limit.
field.capacity.maximum.label: Maximum size
field.capacity.mode.help: Fixed: the size you enter is used. With a fixed size the investment settings are not needed, and the cost of the plant is not part of the system cost. Invest: the optimizer chooses the size that gives the lowest total cost, within the maximum you set.
field.capacity.mode.label: How is the size decided?
field.capacity.opex.help: Yearly maintenance and operation as a percentage of the investment.
field.capacity.opex.label: Running cost
field.conversion.outputs.electricity.eff: The share of the energy put in that comes out as electricity.
The share of the gas energy that comes out as electricity.
field.conversion.outputs.heat.efficiency: The share of the energy put in that comes out as heat.
The share of the gas energy that comes out as heat.
The share of the gas energy that becomes heat.
The share of the electricity that becomes heat.
field.conversion.outputs.heat.ratio.help: The heat that comes out for every unit of electricity put in, for example 3.5.
field.costs.revenue.help: What every kWh earns, for example a feed-in tariff.
field.costs.revenue.help@grid_feedin: What you get for every kWh that you feed into the grid.
field.costs.revenue.label: Revenue
field.costs.variable_costs.help: The cost of every kWh, for example the price of grid electricity.
field.costs.variable_costs.help@gas_impo: What one kWh of gas costs.
field.costs.variable_costs.help@grid: What one kWh from the grid costs.
field.costs.variable_costs.label: Variable costs
field.demand.annual_demand.help: The energy per year. Every hour gets its share of it.
field.demand.annual_demand.help@demand: The electricity per year. Every hour gets its share of it.
field.demand.annual_demand.help@heat_dem: The heat per year. Every hour gets its share of it.
field.demand.annual_demand.label: Annual demand
field.demand.profile_type.help: A normalized profile adds up to 1 over a year: the demand of every hour is its share times the annual demand. An absolute profile already holds the demand in kW.
field.demand.profile_type.label: What does the profile hold?
field.demand.profile_type.option.annual_: Shares that add up to 1 over a year
field.on_off.minimum_downtime.help: Once stopped, it stays off at least this long.
field.on_off.minimum_downtime.label: Minimum off time
field.on_off.minimum_load.help: While running, the component cannot go below this share of its size.
field.on_off.minimum_load.label: Minimum load
field.on_off.minimum_uptime.help: Once started, it runs at least this long.
field.on_off.minimum_uptime.label: Minimum run time
field.on_off.startup_cost.label: Start-up cost
field.storage.c_rate.help: 0.5 means that a full storage can be emptied in two hours.
field.storage.c_rate.label: Charge and discharge power
field.storage.efficiency_charge.help: The share of the energy that arrives in the storage.
field.storage.efficiency_charge.label: Charging efficiency
field.storage.efficiency_discharge.help: The share of the stored energy that comes out.
field.storage.efficiency_discharge.label: Discharging efficiency
field.storage.initial_level.help: The charge level at the start. Leave empty to not fix it.
field.storage.initial_level.label: Initial charge level
field.storage.loss_rate.help: The share of the stored energy that is lost every hour.
field.storage.loss_rate.label: Self-discharge

import.start_outside: The start {start} is outside the file ({first} to {last}).

open.heading: Open a scenario file
open.intro: Or open a scenario that was saved earlier. A scenario file (JSON) holds the components, settings and time series of one energy system. Examples are in the folder examples/scenarios_v2.
result.fixed_note: Components in fixed mode have no capital cost in the optimization.
result.heading: Results
result.help.electricity_consumption: Electricity demand plus electricity used by heat pump and heating rod.
result.help.heat_demand: Heat that has to be supplied.
result.help.own_generation: Electricity from PV, wind and CHP.
result.help.peak_grid_import: Highest power drawn from the grid in a single time step.
result.help.self_consumption: Share of the own generation that is not fed into the grid.
result.help.self_sufficiency: Share of the electricity consumption that is not bought from the grid.
result.help.system_cost: Objective of the optimization: annualised investment and fixed O&M plus energy costs, minus feed-in revenue. Negative means a net revenue.
result.no_capacities: No components with a capacity in this system.
result.no_costs: No cost items in this run.
result.no_flows: This result has no hourly flows.
result.nothing_flows: Nothing flows through this energy carrier in this run.
result.period_note.one: The simulated period is {count} day. Investment costs are annualised (full year), while energy costs cover only the simulated period, so the system cost is not an annual figure.
result.period_note.other: The simulated period is {count} days. Investment costs are annualised (full year), while energy costs cover only the simulated period, so the system cost is not an annual figure.
result.section.costs: Where the system cost comes from
run.failed: The optimization could not be completed: {reason}
run.heading: Run the optimization
run.infeasible: The optimization has no solution: with the components and sizes you chose, the demand cannot be met. Check that something supplies every demand, and that no upper limit or fixed size is too small.
run.intro: The optimization runs in the background, so the page stays usable. A day takes seconds; a whole year of a large system can take several minutes. A week is enough to test that the scenario runs, but the sizes of plants in investment mode need a whole year.
run.no_solution: The optimization found no solution. Either the demand cannot be met with the chosen components and sizes, or a plant without an upper limit would earn money without end. Check the upper limits, the fixed sizes and the feed-in revenue.
run.outdated: You changed the scenario after this run. The results below belong to the earlier version. Run the optimization again to update them.
run.unbounded: The optimization has no limit: as the scenario is set up, the system could earn money without end. Usually a plant without an upper limit (PV or wind) earns more from feeding in than it costs. Set an upper limit for the plant, or lower the feed-in revenue.
run.unexpected: The optimization stopped unexpectedly. Please try again; if it happens again, tell the developers.

scenario.period_hint: The model works in hourly steps: 24 steps are one day, {year} are a year.
series.aggregate.label: What are the values?

series.aggregate.sum: Energy per time step in kWh (the sum of the hour is used)
series.heading: Time series
series.help.demand: One value for each hour. What the values mean (shares of the annual demand, or the demand in kW) is chosen above.
series.help.grid: The price of electricity for each hour. A time series fits a dynamic tariff or spot market prices.
series.help.heat_demand: One value for each hour. What the values mean (shares of the annual demand, or the demand in kW) is chosen above.
series.help.heat_pump: The COP for each hour, for example from the outside temperature. A constant COP is enough for a first estimate.
series.help.pv: The hourly availability of the PV system between 0 and 1 (capacity factor), for example from renewables.ninja.
series.help.wind: The hourly availability of the wind turbine between 0 and 1 (capacity factor), for example from renewables.ninja.
series.preview: Preview: {rows} rows, {columns} columns. The first rows are shown.
series.price_unit: Unit of the prices in the file
series.settings.caption: The layout of the file is detected automatically. Change a setting only if the preview is wrong.
series.settings.header: Line with the column names (0 = none)
series.settings.heading: Import settings
series.start.file: From the first row of the file
series.start.label: Which part of the file is used?
series.start.not_covered: The start of the scenario ({start}) is not in the file. The file is used from its first row.
series.start.scenario: From the start of the scenario ({start})
series.state.waiting: No time series yet. Until you use one, the constant value is used.
